nodes.summary: The proposition that for every finite non-abelian simple group $S$, identified with its inner automorphism group $\mathrm{Inn}(S) \le \mathrm{Aut}(S)$, every subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{Aut}(S)$ containing $S$ is generated by at most $3$ elements.
nodes.title: The 3-generator bound for almost simple groups (Kourovka 11.27)

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is almost simple when there is a nonabelian finite simple group $S$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup $A$ of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(S)$ that contains the inner automorphism group $\mathrm{Inn}(S)$.
nodes.title: Almost simple groups

nodes.summary: For subgroups $G$ and $N$ of a group $A$, the relative generator number of $G$ modulo $N$ is the least $k$ such that some $k$ elements of $A$ together with $N$ generate $G$, and $0$ if no finite set of elements does. For a normal subgroup $N \le G$ with $G / N$ finitely generated it is $d(G / N)$, the minimal number of generators of $G / N$.
